prompt: Some people think that a sense of competition in children should be encouraged. Others believe that children who are taught to co-operate become more useful adults. Discuss both views and give your opinion.
essay:
Encouraging a competitive spirit among young students has become a controversial topic in contemporary society. While it is argued that competition is necessary among young children, the opposing view is that cooperation can benefit them more in the long run. In my view, the latter claim is more valid than the former one.This essay will discuss both views and give the explanation of why I believe so.

There are several upsides of nudging young students to be competitive. First and foremost, it is maintained that competition is a source of motivation for them. In other words, it can act as a catalyst for them to strive for excellence in their academic journey. For instance, some students come out on top of the class due to their competitive spirit. Moreover, those well-rounded students can inspire their peers to work hard. By seeing the progress of top students, other students aspire to fulfil their potential.

On the other hand, there is the opposing view that children benefit more from learning how to work collaboratively, which I agree with. Firstly, it can help develop team spirit in youngsters, which is one of the essential life skills in the modern workplace. To illustrate, there is project-based learning in some schools, where students have to work in a team. It is imperative to delegate responsibilities and lend a hand to each other to accomplish it successfully, which partly contributes to their overall grades. As they can see how a supportive environment can benefit them in hand, there is a strong likelihood that they adopt that mannerism.

Moreover, competition can sometimes do more harm than good. It can pressurise young kids to win at all costs. As long as the results are good, they tend to ignore moral values and beliefs.Cheating in exams is a case. Bitter rivalry forces them to do the wrong things that can breach their academic integrity. Sports competitions in schools are also a point, where young athletes do not play fair and square in order to gain a competitive edge. In these cases, even though a desirable outcome can be achieved, it is impossible for them to hold their heads up, and this can lead to joyless accomplishment.

To conclude, it is claimed by some that competitive children make students better academically, whereas I tend to agree with the opposite idea that working cooperatively can bring more positive impacts on students and their future lives. I believe schools can shape the future of young students if cooperation is prioritised.
